topic: Bodi Takes Insanity Into the Hyrox Era

facts.label: Story
facts.value: Bodi Takes Insanity Into the Hyrox Era

facts.label: Article
facts.value: One of home fitness’s original players wants in on the hybrid racing boom, giving at-home exercisers a way to train for Hyrox and hybrid fitness events As gyms race to keep pace with the boom in Hyrox and other hybrid fitness events , Bodi is making its play from the living room. The company formerly known as Beachbody has launched Insanity: Unhinged, a 100-day hybrid training program led by three-time Hyrox world champion Hunter McIntyre and executive produced by Shaun T, the trainer who created the original Insanity. The new program mixes cardio, strength, speed and conditioning, ideal for those preparing for Hyrox and other fitness competitions, along with anyone curious to see how far they can push themselves. “This isn’t just another workout program,” said Carl Daikeler, Bodi’s co-founder and CEO . “It’s a 100-day plan that balances getting familiar with new moves — then unleashing your ‘unhinged’ intensity from week to week.” Hunter McIntyre (credit: Bodi) Participants train seven days a week across 45 workouts split into three progressive phases. Weekday sessions run 30 to 45 minutes and rotate through five formats: Upper Body Power, Metabolic Conditioning, Engine Work, Overdrive and Upper Body Strength. Saturdays bring a 45-minute Competition Day that tests strength, conditioning and mental toughness, while Sundays are set aside for recovery.

en.headline: Bodi Takes Insanity Into the Hyrox Era

topic: YouFit Gyms Launches $10 Million-Plus Club Reinvestment Backed by Skyline Investors

facts.label: Story
facts.value: YouFit Gyms Launches $10 Million-Plus Club Reinvestment Backed by Skyline Investors

facts.label: Article
facts.value: YouFit Gyms announced a $10 million-plus investment from Skyline Investors , a Los Angeles-based private equity firm. The capital will be reinvested into existing clubs to refresh and elevate the brand and support strategic growth. The deal marks Skyline Investors’ first investment in the fitness and wellness space. The first phase of the reinvestment will include 12 club refreshes across Florida. Each refresh centers on reimagining the workout floor with an updated aesthetic, new equipment and broader amenity set to elevate the member experience. As the fitness consumer has shifted from a focus on cardio to strength training, YouFit is expanding its strength floors to match member demand. The refreshes will also add recovery modalities and build out expanded functional training space with a broader range of equipment. YouFit plans to reinvest across its entire portfolio, with this initial phase marking the first step of a longer-term brand enhancement. “Upon joining YouFit, I saw a brand with a proud history, loyal members, and great clubs that did not have the resources to grow,” said Jason Carter, the CEO of YouFit Gyms. “To secure this investment is validating for our team.

topic: LEVL Strength introduces isokinetic home training

facts.label: Story
facts.value: LEVL Strength introduces isokinetic home training

facts.label: Article
facts.value: Without a barbell or weight rack, building serious strength at home can be difficult, but LEVL Strength aims to change that. LEVL brings heavy resistance training into a compact, portable home system. The portable, adjustable machine packs up to 500 pounds of magnetic resistance into a compact system, bringing heavy resistance training into the home. There’s no installation, no setup, and no bulky weights cluttering your space. Not only does the machine eliminate the need for physical weights, it also adapts to the user. In Isokinetic, or “Iso-K Mode,” LEVL responds to your force output in real time, adjusting resistance to match your strength throughout every movement and every rep. LEVL cites this as a “weak spot” in traditional strength training. Force production fluctuates throughout a movement, meaning some portions of an exercise can feel considerably easier or more challenging than others. LEVL claims its adaptive resistance technology can deliver an effective strength workout in as few as five reps per exercise. By dynamically adjusting resistance to keep muscles challenged throughout the entire range of motion, the machine aims to make every rep count. Think of a bicep curl: the bottom portion might feel effortless, while the middle feels like your arm is climbing Mount Everest. This also makes the process of choosing a weight much easier.

topic: Peloton Draws $6.8 Billion Demand for Debut Junk-Bond Sale

facts.label: Story
facts.value: Peloton Draws $6.8 Billion Demand for Debut Junk-Bond Sale

facts.label: Article
facts.value: The offering drew more than $6.8 billion of orders and was upsized by $100 million to $700 million, according to people familiar with the matter. (Bloomberg) — Peloton Interactive Inc. has attracted strong investor demand for its debut junk-bond sale, allowing the fitness company to boost the deal’s size and slash borrowing costs. The offering drew more than $6.8 billion of orders and was upsized by $100 million to $700 million, according to people familiar with the matter. The notes, due in 2032, were sold at par to yield 8.63%, compared with initial talk in the low-to-mid 9% area, the people said, asking not to be identified because they’re not authorized to speak publicly. The bond sale hit investors just a few days after Peloton forecast quarterly revenue that topped analyst projections, in a sign that efforts to turn around the business are making progress. The deal also offered buyers a sizeable yield premium over the 6.85% average for similarly rated bonds. Peloton, which saw sales surge during the pandemic lockdowns, has since grappled with management shakeups and excess inventory. It has now bet on artificial intelligence-powered software, redesigned hardware and new partnerships to drum up demand. “Peloton’s earnings and free cash flow have significantly improved following extensive restructuring ,” Moody’s Ratings said in a Monday note to clients.

en.headline: Peloton Draws $6.8 Billion Demand for Debut Junk-Bond Sale
